title: The corner, iii
logline: Friday, week two. The hardware store's sale sign in the background of a strip about the dog's vet appointment. EVERYTHING MUST GO, behind the Datsun, unremarked. The strip is about the dog.

panels.composition: Main street. The Datsun at the curb. WOOD lifting BARNABY, eleven, into it. Behind: Wagner's window, a sign — EVERYTHING MUST GO — half visible.

characters.pose: lifting the dog into the car

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man lifting an old dog into a rusted car at a curb while a hardware store's window behind shows a half-visible closing-sale sign
image.notes: Letter after: EVERYTHING MUST GO, partly cut by the car. The strip's subject is the dog.

panels.composition: The dog on the seat. The vet's card on the dash.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of an old dog on a car seat with a vet's appointment card on the dashboard

panels.composition: Wood at the wheel. In the mirror: Wagner's. A man carrying a ladder out of it. Unremarked.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man driving with a hardware store visible in his mirror where a man carries a ladder out the door, no words

panels.composition: The car pulling away. The corner. The sign, whole now, in the window behind, as the car leaves the panel. The strip still about the dog.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a rusted car leaving a street corner with a hardware store's closing-sale sign fully visible in the window behind, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: EVERYTHING MUST GO, behind the dog's vet trip.
